name: Bradford Woodworking
old_description: Founded in 1980 by master craftsman Brad Smith on the Worcester, Pennsylvania farm where he was raised, Bradford Woodworking creates “farm fresh furniture” that transforms everyday farm tools into something special and much greater than their parts.
about:
Bradford Woodworking was founded in 1980 by master craftsman Brad Smith on the Worcester, Pennsylvania farm where he was raised. The business began as a one-man operation on his family farm, turning everyday farm tools into distinctive furniture pieces.

Today, the company produces hand-crafted furniture and home goods including stools, benches, tables, and small luxury items. Each piece is made by Smith using traditional woodworking techniques such as lathe turning and hand joinery, with select components like tractor seats sourced from Amish forges. The workshop operates on the original farm property, though the company also fulfills wholesale orders through the Faire marketplace.

Bradford Woodworking serves both retail customers and wholesale buyers, with products ranging from entryway benches and dining stools to baby furniture and kitchen accessories. Retailers stock their goods via Faire Direct, while individual clients commission custom pieces directly with Smith.

The brand’s differentiation lies in its “farm fresh furniture” concept—repurposing agricultural implements into heirloom-quality pieces. Smith has stated that the venture began from a desire to transform utilitarian farm tools into objects that are “something special and much greater than their parts.”
